memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Moses placed the table in the tent of meeting on the north side of the tabernacle outside the curtain and set out the bread on it before the Lord, as the Lord commanded him. He placed the lampstand in the tent of meeting opposite the table on the south side of the tabernacle and set up the lamps before the Lord, as the Lord commanded him." - Exod 40:22-25 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Bread on one side, light on the other, facing each other across the holy place.

The bread was called the bread of the Presence — twelve loaves, one for each tribe, set out fresh every Sabbath (Lev 24:5-8). The lamps burned continually.

Nourishment and light. Both maintained. Both before the Lord.

Jesus took up both images and applied them to Himself. "I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will never go hungry" (John 6:35). "I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will never walk in darkness" (John 8:12).

That is not coincidence. The furniture of the holy place was preparing Israel to recognise Him.

Notice that the bread was set out "before the Lord." It was not primarily for the priests to eat, though they did. It was placed in God's presence — a picture of God's people continually before Him.

And notice both had to be maintained. Fresh bread weekly. Lamps trimmed daily. Neither was a one-time arrangement.

Our souls work the same way. Yesterday's bread does not feed today. A lamp lit last month is not burning now.

What are you doing this week to be fed and to stay lit?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you feeding on Christ regularly or living off old meals?
2. Has your light been quietly dimming without a dramatic failure?
3. What daily or weekly rhythm keeps you nourished?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You are my bread and my light. Feed me today and keep me burning clearly. Amen.
